To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of serum IgM, IgG and IgM to selected protein and nonprotein antigens provides promising diagnostic signatures to differentiate active TB disease from LTBI and other respiratory diseases in a TB endemic setting.

the combined detection of serum IgA, IgM and/or IgG antibodies to selected mycobacteria-specific targets (LAM and 7 protein antigens) provides promising diagnostic signatures to differentiate active TB from other diseases with similar signs and symptoms in TB endemic regions.
the combined use of IgA, and IgM antibodies against selected myco-bacterial antigens can improve the specificity and sensitivity of TB diagnostics in TB-endemic regions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a serodiagnostic test to differentiate active TB from other pulmonary diseases in endemic areas, which could potentially be used as a triage test to reduce the burden of TB diagnostic work-ups.
the identification of novel biomarkers that can improve the diagnostic performance of serological tests for active TB.
developing novel serodiagnostic tests for the detection of active TB disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of 3 or more IgG, IgA or IgM antibodies against 16 kDa, MPT64 and LAM is a promising serological test for the detection of active TB disease in TB endemic settings.
the combined detection of anti-tuberculosis IgG, IgA and IgM antibodies in a single assay is promising to improve TB diagnosis in primary health care clinics in TB endemic regions.
the use of a panel of antibodies in combination with other TB diagnostic tools could provide a promising diagnostic tool for the diagnosis of TB.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of anti-LAM IgG and anti-16 kDA IgA antibodies is a promising serodiagnostic signature for active TB.

a combined use of IgM and/or IgA responses against LAM and 4 mycobacterial protein targets (16 kDa, MPT64 and Tpx) provides a highly sensitive and specific serological signature to differentiate between active TB and LTBI.
the combined use of 16 kD IgA, 16kD IgM and MPT64 IgA as well as LAM IgG, TB-LTIB IgG and 16kD-IgM in combination with a single antigen (16 kD) can be a useful diagnostic tool in TB endemic areas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combined use of different antibodies to different mycobacterial targets may be a promising approach to increase the specificity of TB serodiagnostic tests.

the combined use of 2 or 3 Ig classes to a limited number of mycobacterial targets can improve the diagnostic accuracy of serological tests to differentiate active TB from other pulmonary diseases in a TB endemic region.
a combined analysis of IgG, IgM and IgM antibodies against a panel of selected antigens provides a promising diagnostic signature for active TB in a primary care setting.
